title: KCS v6 Practices Guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Solve Loop practices (capture, structure, reuse, improve) with the techniques 'Search Early Search Often' and 'Flag It or Fix It'; Evolve Loop practices (content health, process integration, performance assessment, leadership and communication).

title: About omnichannel routing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Routing by status and capacity, most spare capacity or round robin, custom queues checked first, skills and skills timeout, priority and soonest-SLA-breach ordering; features by plan (Team, Growth, Professional with up to 5 custom statuses, Enterprise up to 100).

title: About intelligent triage
supports: Opened with WebFetch (article updated 19 Oct 2026 per the help centre search API). Detects topic, sentiment, language and custom entities on tickets with a public comment; classifications on Suite and Support Professional and above; using them in workflows such as routing triggers needs the Copilot add-on.

title: Defining SLA policies
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Targets based on the system Priority field; blank priority means no SLA; custom priority fields cannot carry targets; reply, update and resolution metrics; choose one resolution metric; most restrictive policies at the top; plan requirements.

title: Understanding SLA Policies
supports: Opened with WebFetch (modified 20 Aug 2026). First matching policy applies; first response time excludes automation 'Send Reply' actions; targets per priority in business or calendar hours; multiple policies and breach escalations from the Pro plan.

title: About automations and how they work
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 30 Oct 2026). Triggers run on create or update, automations run hourly; nullifying condition needed to avoid loops; limits of 500 active automations and 1,000 tickets per automation per hour; standard automation closes tickets 96 hours after solved.

title: About Zendesk sandbox environments
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 2 Nov 2026). Sandbox changes do not affect production; copies settings, triggers, automations, macros and up to 10,000 tickets; plan availability and add-on; emails changed to @example.com; changes must be recreated manually in production.

title: Determining your staffing requirements for voice support
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Recommends the Erlang C calculator; inputs (calls per hour, handling time including wrap-up, percentage within maximum wait, maximum wait); worked example of 30 calls an hour and 300 seconds giving six agents; the formula is only a guide and ignores breaks and shifts.

title: Best practices for forecasting staffing needs
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 4 Nov 2026). Up to two years of history, cut-off dates, exclude outliers, manual adjustments for events; Erlang C may give slightly higher staffing for low-volume workstreams; email outside hours moves to the next period while live-channel volume outside hours is disregarded; compare forecast with actual.

title: Creating scorecards
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 4 Nov 2026). Category weights 0 to 100 (default 10); critical categories fail the review or group below 50%; binary to 5-point scales; optional N/A and root causes; needs the QA or WFM add-on.

title: How does AutoQA evaluate tickets?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 28 Apr 2026). Scores closed or solved tickets with at least one customer and one agent message of 10+ words; skips tickets imported before the scorecard was published and spam.

title: About article verification and how it works
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 7 Jul 2026). Verification rules remind article owners on schedules (examples from 2 weeks to 1 year); unverified articles stay on a needs-verification list; Enterprise plans.

title: Getting started with self-service, Part 7: Maintaining and improving your knowledge base
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Archive articles no longer relevant after checking they are not still searched for and used; fix or redirect links first; owners and scheduled reviews on Enterprise.

title: What is the difference between first reply time and requester wait time metrics?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 16 Jun 2026). First reply time runs to the first public agent comment; requester wait time counts New, Open and On-hold statuses.

title: Why is the First reply time higher than the Full resolution time on my Support dashboard?
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 3 Nov 2026). First reply time is filtered on ticket created date and full resolution time on ticket solved date, so they cover different ticket sets and cannot be compared directly.

title: Fin AI Agent resolutions
supports: Opened with WebFetch (dated 23 Sep 2026). Confirmed versus assumed resolutions; not counted if the customer asks for a person or follows up; one outcome per conversation; billed per resolution (price not quoted in this kit).

title: Intercom MCP server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Read tools for conversations, contacts, companies and articles; add_internal_note cannot send customer-visible replies; create and update articles; no listed tool changes assignment or tags; US and EU regions, AU not yet supported; OAuth recommended.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration in Freshdesk
supports: Opened with WebFetch (modified 5 Oct 2026). Freshworks MCP server for Claude, Cursor and other MCP clients; read, create, update and reply to tickets, add notes, solution articles; API key authentication only; action limits by plan; generally available 10 Sep 2026.

title: Email AI Agent setup and configuration
supports: Opened with WebFetch (modified 9 Jul 2026). Drafts replies from knowledge sources, resolves or escalates; handover rules and multi-turn limits; optional mandatory disclaimer footer on every AI reply; preview and bulk evaluate modes that do not affect live conversations. The page includes sample instructions written for the product's own AI agent, treated as page content only.

title: Klarna AI assistant handles two-thirds of customer service chats in its first month
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Company claims (February 2024): 2.3 million conversations, two-thirds of chats, resolution under 2 minutes from 11, repeat inquiries down 25%, customers can still choose live agents.

title: AI Act, Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
supports: Opened with WebFetch (text based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version as at 27 July 2026). Providers must design systems that interact directly with people so they know it is AI unless obvious; information clear and distinguishable, at the latest at the first interaction.

title: Transparency obligations under Article 50 of the AI Act (questions and answers)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 24 Jul 2026). Applies from 2 August 2026; chatbots and AI agents covered; 'obvious' exception read restrictively; no grace period for chatbot disclosure (only Article 50(2) marking to 2 Dec 2026); fines up to EUR 15 million or 3% of worldwide turnover.

title: Using AI agents: complying with consumer law
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 30 Oct 2026). Businesses responsible for AI agents as for employees, including third-party agents; label where it could affect decisions and do not let customers think a person is serving them; human in the loop; test and monitor; fines up to 10% of worldwide turnover.

title: Time limits for businesses
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 8 weeks for most complaints, 15 days for payment services, e-money and fraud or scam complaints; final or holding response; final response must state the 6-month referral right and include the leaflet.

title: Telecoms and pay-TV complaints
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 26 Oct 2026). Q2 2026 complaints by provider; for fixed broadband, BT, EE, TalkTalk and Vodafone had the most complaints and Plusnet, Sky and Virgin Media the fewest.

title: Site relocation: Online Dispute Resolution platform discontinued
supports: Opened with WebFetch (reached by redirect from the old ODR address). The EU ODR platform was discontinued as of 20 July 2025 following Regulation (EU) 2024/3228; points to national dispute resolution bodies.

title: Deleting tickets
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 1 May 2026). Deleted tickets stay 30 days in the Deleted tickets view, then are permanently deleted automatically; permanent deletion cannot be undone and removes attachments; some teams close tickets through automations instead.

title: Respect individuals' rights (SME data protection guide)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Reply within one month, extendable by two months with notice; right of access free of charge; erasure conditions and limited grounds to refuse; identity checks where in reasonable doubt.

title: Data protection basics (SME data protection guide)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Storage limitation: keep data only as long as necessary, then delete or anonymise; internal retention periods by purpose and a deletion procedure; data minimisation.

title: UK Customer Satisfaction Index (UKCSI)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. July 2026 UKCSI 78.3, up 1 point on July 2025; 59,500 responses covering 277 organisations or organisation types across 13 sectors; sector scores.
